claims.text: Refining the microstructure to a fine-grained state can enhance high-temperature plastic strain capacity in fusion plasma-facing structural materials.
Refining the microstructure to a fine-grained state can enhance toughness in fusion plasma-facing structural materials.
Reducing grain size increases grain-boundary density.
The increased grain-boundary density limits deleterious dislocation motion.
The increased grain-boundary density limits grain-boundary sliding.
Severe plastic deformation or optimized heat treatment can produce controlled grain-size reduction.
Temperatures above 1000°C are representative high-temperature conditions for the proposed fusion-reactor simulation.
Grain boundaries act as barriers that influence dislocation arrangements.
Impeded dislocation motion and reduced grain-boundary sliding delay the onset of localized deformation.
Delaying localized deformation enhances plastic strain capacity and toughness.
Fine-grained samples will exhibit greater plastic strain before failure than coarse-grained samples under otherwise identical high-temperature loading.
Fine-grained samples will exhibit greater toughness than coarse-grained samples under otherwise identical high-temperature loading.
The proposed mechanism applies to tungsten-based alloys and steels at high temperature when oxidation and radiation-induced microstructural changes are minimal.
